chronology.label: Birth
chronology.detail: Born in Katsushika district of Edo, Japan; childhood name was Tokitarō

chronology.label: Started painting
chronology.detail: Began painting around age six

chronology.label: Age 12, sent to bookshop
chronology.detail: Father sent him to work in a bookshop and lending library

chronology.label: Age 14, apprenticed
chronology.detail: Worked as apprentice to a woodcarver

chronology.label: Age 18, entered Shunshō's studio
chronology.detail: Entered studio of Katsukawa Shunshō, master of ukiyo-e and head of Katsukawa school

chronology.label: First name change: Shunrō
chronology.detail: Dubbed Shunrō by his master; published first prints, a series of kabuki actors

chronology.label: First wife died
chronology.detail: Death of first wife; very little known about her

chronology.label: Death of Shunshō
chronology.detail: Master Shunshō died; Hokusai began exploring other styles including European approaches

chronology.label: Expelled from Katsukawa school
chronology.detail: Expelled by Shunkō, chief disciple of Shunshō, possibly for studying at rival Kanō school

chronology.label: Second marriage
chronology.detail: Married second wife; she also died after a short time

chronology.label: Name change: Hokusai Tomisa
chronology.detail: Passed his name to a pupil and adopted name Hokusai Tomisa as independent artist, free from school ties

chronology.label: Adopted name: Katsushika Hokusai
chronology.detail: Adopted the name he would be most widely known by; published Famous Sights of the Eastern Capital and Eight Views of Edo

chronology.label: Created enormous Daruma portrait
chronology.detail: During Edo festival, created enormous portrait of Buddhist prelate Daruma, said to be 200 square meters

chronology.label: Collaboration with Takizawa Bakin
chronology.detail: Collaborated with popular novelist on series of illustrated books

chronology.label: Chinsetsu Yumiharizuki published
chronology.detail: Fantasy novel illustrated by Hokusai; main character Minamoto no Tametomo

chronology.label: Name change: Taito
chronology.detail: At age 51, changed name to Taito; entered period creating Hokusai Manga and art manuals

chronology.label: Quick Lessons in Simplified Drawing published
chronology.detail: First art manual intended to make money and attract students

chronology.label: Hokusai Manga volume 1 published
chronology.detail: First volume of Manga; immediate success; included thousands of drawings

chronology.label: Kinoe no Komatsu published
chronology.detail: Three-volume book of shunga (erotic art); includes The Dream of the Fisherman's Wife

chronology.label: Great Daruma in Nagoya
chronology.detail: Painted enormous Great Daruma outside Hongan-ji Nagoya Betsuin; 18 × 10.8 metres; drew huge crowds; received name Darusen/Daruma Master

chronology.label: Name change: Iitsu
chronology.detail: Changed name to Iitsu; marked start of period securing fame throughout Japan

chronology.label: Hokusai Manga: 12 volumes produced
chronology.detail: By this year, 12 volumes completed; 3 more published posthumously

chronology.label: Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji series
chronology.detail: Most celebrated work; proved popular; 10 more prints added to series; includes The Great Wave off Kanagawa and Red Fuji

chronology.label: A True Mirror of Chinese and Japanese Poetry
chronology.detail: Printed in extra-long vertical formats; included poems with scenes; 10 designs survive

chronology.label: Name change: Gakyō Rōjin Manji
chronology.detail: Beginning in this year, worked under name meaning The Old Man Mad About Art; produced One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji

chronology.label: One Hundred Poems Explained by a Nurse
chronology.detail: Final print series; never published in full, possibly due to financial hardships

chronology.label: Fire destroyed studio
chronology.detail: Fire destroyed Hokusai's studio and much of his work; career beginning to fade

chronology.label: Daily lion paintings
chronology.detail: Painted Chinese lions (shishi) every morning in ink on paper as daily exorcisms/talisman against misfortune

chronology.label: Feminine Wave created
chronology.detail: Painted while living in Obuse

chronology.label: Late works
chronology.detail: Painted The Dragon of Smoke Escaping from Mt Fuji and Tiger in the Snow in early 1849

chronology.label: Death
chronology.detail: Died at age 88; buried at Seikyō-ji in Tokyo (Taito Ward)

quotes.text: What really motivated the development of my artistic style was the embarrassment I suffered at Shunkō's hands
quotes.speaker: Hokusai
quotes.context: After being expelled from the Katsukawa school by Shunkō

quotes.text: From the age of six, I had a passion for copying the form of things and since the age of fifty I have published many drawings, yet of all I drew by my seventieth year there is nothing worth taking into account. At seventy-three years I partly understood the structure of animals, birds, insects and fishes, and the life of grasses and plants. And so, at eighty-six I shall progress further; at ninety I shall even further penetrate their secret meaning, and by one hundred I shall perhaps truly have reached the level of the marvellous and divine. When I am one hundred and ten, each dot, each line will possess a life of its own.
quotes.speaker: Hokusai
quotes.context: From the colophon of One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji

quotes.text: If only Heaven will give me just another ten years ... Just another five more years, then I could become a real painter
quotes.speaker: Hokusai

quotes.text: Though as a ghost, I shall lightly tread, the summer fields
quotes.speaker: Hokusai
quotes.context: Haiku composed shortly before his death

quotes.text: Hokusai is not just one artist among others in the Floating World. He is an island, a continent, a whole world in himself
quotes.speaker: Edgar Degas
quotes.context: Speaking about Hokusai's influence and significance

people.name: Katsushika Hokusai
people.role: Japanese ukiyo-e artist, painter, and printmaker of the Edo period

people.name: Nakajima Ise
people.role: Hokusai's father; mirror-maker for the shōgun

people.name: Tokitarō
people.role: Hokusai's childhood name at birth

people.name: Katsukawa Shunshō
people.role: Hokusai's first master at age 18; head of Katsukawa school; artist of ukiyo-e focusing on courtesans and kabuki actors

people.name: Shunkō
people.role: Chief disciple of Shunshō; expelled Hokusai from the Katsukawa school

people.name: Hokusai's first wife
people.role: Married during Hokusai's decade in Shunshō's studio; died in early 1790s

people.name: Hokusai's second wife
people.role: Married in 1797; died shortly after marriage

people.name: Ei (also known as Ōi)
people.role: Hokusai's youngest daughter; became an artist and his assistant

people.name: Takizawa Bakin
people.role: Popular novelist; collaborated with Hokusai on illustrated books 1804-1815

people.name: Minamoto no Tametomo
people.role: Main character in Chinsetsu Yumiharizuki (Strange Tales of the Crescent Moon)

people.name: Egawa Tomekichi
people.role: Blockcutter who worked with Hokusai; Hokusai respected his work

people.name: Sugita Kinsuke
people.role: Blockcutter who worked with Hokusai on Toshisen Ehon

people.name: Sesshū Tōyō
people.role: Influenced Hokusai's artistic style

people.name: Andō Hiroshige
people.role: Younger artist who became increasingly popular, causing Hokusai's career to fade by 1839

people.name: Takai Kozan
people.role: Wealthy farmer who invited 83-year-old Hokusai to Obuse in Shinano Province

people.name: Keisai Eisen
people.role: Disciple of Hokusai; painted his portrait

people.name: Vincent van Gogh
people.role: Western artist influenced by Hokusai's works during wave of Japonisme

people.name: Claude Monet
people.role: Western artist influenced by Hokusai's works during wave of Japonisme

people.name: Francois-Eugene Rousseau

people.name: Edgar Degas
people.role: European artist who collected Hokusai's woodcuts; praised him

people.name: Paul Gauguin
people.role: European artist who collected Hokusai's woodcuts

people.name: Gustav Klimt
people.role: European artist who collected Hokusai's woodcuts

people.name: Franz Marc
people.role: European artist who collected Hokusai's woodcuts

people.name: August Macke
people.role: European artist who collected Hokusai's woodcuts

people.name: Édouard Manet
people.role: European artist influenced by Hokusai; collected his woodcuts

people.name: Claude Debussy

people.name: Roger Zelazny

people.name: Hermann Obrist
people.role: Artist whose whiplash motif was visibly influenced by Hokusai's work

places.name: Katsushika district
places.significance: District of Edo where Hokusai was born; inspired his adopted name Katsushika Hokusai

places.name: Edo
places.significance: Capital of the Tokugawa shogunate; Hokusai's birthplace; current Tokyo

places.name: Tokyo
places.significance: Present-day name for Edo; contains Taito Ward where Hokusai was buried at Seikyō-ji

places.name: Taito Ward
places.significance: District in Tokyo where Hokusai was buried at Seikyō-ji temple

places.name: Mount Fuji
places.significance: Major subject of Hokusai's most famous works; inspiration for multiple series

places.name: Ryogoku Bridge
places.significance: Location depicted in print Fireworks in the Cool of Evening at Ryogoku Bridge in Edo

places.name: Kanagawa
places.significance: Location featured in The Great Wave off Kanagawa, Hokusai's most iconic print

places.name: Nagoya
places.significance: Location where Hokusai painted the Great Daruma on 5 October 1817

places.name: Hongan-ji Nagoya Betsuin
places.significance: Temple where Hokusai painted the enormous Great Daruma measuring 18 × 10.8 metres

places.name: Obuse
places.significance: Town in Shinano Province (now Nagano Prefecture) where 83-year-old Hokusai stayed several years; created Masculine and Feminine Wave there

places.name: Shinano Province
places.significance: Now Nagano Prefecture; location of Obuse where Hokusai spent later years

places.name: Paris
places.significance: City where Japanese art including Hokusai's work was first collected c. 1856; hosted Universal Exposition in 1867 featuring Rousseau Service inspired by Hokusai

places.name: Europe
places.significance: Region where Hokusai's works had significant influence during wave of Japonisme in late 19th century; influenced Impressionism and Art Nouveau

places.name: Seikyō-ji
places.significance: Temple in Tokyo (Taito Ward) where Hokusai was buried

places.name: British Museum
places.significance: Holds Hokusai's Great Picture Book of Everything; exhibited his later year artworks including The Great Wave in 2017

places.name: Tokyo National Museum
places.significance: Held major Hokusai exhibition in 2005 with largest number of visitors of any exhibit that year

works.title: Kabuki actors series
works.note: First prints published under name Shunrō

works.title: Courtesan Asleep
works.note: Bijin-ga surimono print

works.title: Fireworks in the Cool of Evening at Ryogoku Bridge in Edo
works.note: Print from period working in Shunshō's studio

works.title: Famous Sights of the Eastern Capital
works.note: Landscape collection published

works.title: Eight Views of Edo
works.note: Landscape collection published

works.title: Chinsetsu Yumiharizuki
works.note: Fantasy novel also known as Strange Tales of the Crescent Moon; illustrated by Hokusai in collaboration with novelist Takizawa Bakin

works.title: Quick Lessons in Simplified Drawing
works.note: Art manual intended to make money and attract students

works.title: Hokusai Manga
works.note: Random drawings featuring thousands of drawings of objects, plants, animals, religious figures, and everyday people; first volume published 1814 as immediate success

works.title: Kinoe no Komatsu
works.note: Three-volume book of shunga (erotic art); includes The Dream of the Fisherman's Wife

works.title: The Dream of the Fisherman's Wife
works.note: Shunga print depicting young woman entwined with octopuses; most famous image in erotic art genre; included in Kinoe no Komatsu

works.title: Toshisen Ehon
works.note: Japanese edition of anthology of Chinese poetry

works.title: Great Daruma
works.note: Ink on paper portrait painted outside Hongan-ji Nagoya Betsuin; 18 × 10.8 metres; drew huge crowds; original destroyed 1945 but handbills preserved at Nagoya City Museum

works.title: Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji
works.note: Most celebrated work; created as response to domestic travel boom and personal interest in Mount Fuji; proved very popular; 10 additional prints later added to original series

works.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
works.note: Most famous print; first in series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji; iconic ukiyo-e work

works.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning
works.note: Also known as Red Fuji; from Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji series; secured fame both in Japan and overseas

works.title: A Tour of the Waterfalls of the Provinces
works.note: Popular print series from period when Hokusai was under name Iitsu

works.title: Oceans of Wisdom
works.note: Popular print series from period when Hokusai was under name Iitsu

works.title: Unusual Views of Celebrated Bridges in the Provinces
works.note: Popular print series from period when Hokusai was under name Iitsu

works.title: Poppies
works.note: Extraordinarily detailed image of flowers and birds (kachō-e)

works.title: Flock of Chickens
works.note: Extraordinarily detailed image of flowers and birds (kachō-e)

works.title: A True Mirror of Chinese and Japanese Poetry
works.note: Also known as Shika shashin kyo; printed in extra-long vertical formats like Chinese hand scrolls; includes poems combined with scenes and scenes from Noh plays; ten designs survive

works.title: One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji
works.note: Significant landscape series created under name Gakyō Rōjin Manji; generally considered masterpiece among his landscape picture books

works.title: One Hundred Poems Explained by a Nurse
works.note: Also known as Hyakunin isshu tuba ga etoki; final print series; never published in full, possibly due to financial hardships

works.title: Hokusai's Great Picture Book of Everything
works.note: Set of drawings; never made into book so drawings never destroyed as typically happened in woodblock process; focuses on Buddhist India, ancient China, and natural world; now in British Museum

works.title: Masculine Wave
works.note: Created while Hokusai was living in Obuse

works.title: Feminine Wave
works.note: Painted while Hokusai was living in Obuse

works.title: The Dragon of Smoke Escaping from Mt Fuji
works.note: Painting created in early 1849

works.title: Tiger in the Snow
works.note: Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk; created in early 1849

works.title: Store Selling Picture Books and Ukiyo-e
works.note: Shows how ukiyo-e was sold at local shops; demonstrates hand-colored approach rather than multiple woodblocks

names.name: Shunrō
names.period/meaning: First art name; adopted after one year studying with Katsukawa Shunshō; used for first published prints in 1779

names.name: Tawaraya Sōri
names.period/meaning: Associated with Tawaraya School; used during middle period

names.name: Hokusai Tomisa
names.period/meaning: Adopted 1798 when he became independent artist, free from school ties; passed previous name to a pupil

names.name: Katsushika Hokusai
names.period/meaning: Adopted by 1800; the name he would be most widely known by; Katsushika refers to district of Edo where he was born; Hokusai means north studio in honor of the North Star, symbol of deity important in Nichiren Buddhism

names.name: Taito
names.period/meaning: Adopted 1811 at age 51; marked start of period creating Hokusai Manga and art manuals

names.name: Iitsu
names.period/meaning: Adopted 1820; change marked start of period in which he secured fame as artist throughout Japan

names.name: Gakyō Rōjin Manji
names.period/meaning: Japanese 画狂老人卍; The Old Man Mad About Art; used beginning 1834; period in which he produced One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji
